citation.title: Components of sensorimotor adaptation in young and elderly subjects

parsed.eligibility_rationale: Upper-extremity visuomotor rotation adaptation with young vs old groups and both adaptation and after-effect phases: "Twelve young and twelve old subjects executed center-out pointing movements while visual feedback about their fingertip was either veridical (baseline), 60-deg rotated (adaptation), or absent (after-effect)." Written in English.
parsed.design_notes: Single pointing-adaptation experiment. Experimental subjects (12 young, 12 old) completed baseline, 15 adaptation episodes (+60 deg rotation), 5 after-effect episodes (no feedback), 3 refresh episodes (rotation re-instated), then 10 transfer tracking episodes with rotated feedback — the refresh and tracking-transfer phases are repeated/later exposures in the same participants and are not independent contrasts (dataset rules 1-2), so only the initial pointing adaptation and its immediately following after-effect phase are used. A separate control sample (12 young, 12 old naive subjects) performed tracking only, never the pointing task, so it provides no pointing adaptation/aftereffect data; the tracking transfer phase also involves a task/context change (pointing -> tracking) and is excluded under dataset rule 3. Ns are consistent between Methods and the ANOVA degrees of freedom for pointing (F(1,22)); the tracking transfer ANOVA reports F(1,43), implying one participant's data may be missing from that (excluded) analysis. Figures 1 and 2 both use triangles for young and squares for old, matching the text groups; Fig. 2 x-axis is labelled "pointing episode" though it plots tracking episodes (apparent labelling error).

Those subjects only executed ten tracking episodes with veridical feedback on the first day and five tracking episodes with +60° rotated feedback"
all_groups_listed.notes: No pointing task; tracking only — not used for protocol outcomes.

all_groups_listed.label: old control subjects (tracking only)
all_groups_listed.n_evidence: "we recruited additional twelve young (22.6±1.9 years of age) and twelve old (72.5±6.0 years of age) healthy and naïve volunteers."
all_groups_listed.notes: No pointing task; tracking only — not used for protocol outcomes.

all_groups_listed.label: pooled seniors sample for correlation analysis
all_groups_listed.n_evidence: "In effect, our sample size thus increased to 54 seniors aged 64.0±4.5 years, all healthy and naïve to the experiment."
all_groups_listed.notes: Includes seniors from two previous unpublished experiments; used only for trail-making/adaptation correlation, no young comparison.

datasets.chosen_pair_rationale: The only pair that performed the pointing adaptation and after-effect phases is the experimental young (26.0±5.0 y) and older (69.5±7.5 y) groups. The tracking-only control young/old groups were not chosen because they never experienced the pointing perturbation, and the pooled 54-senior correlation sample was not chosen because it has no matched young group.
datasets.notes: Outcomes available: late_adaptation from the final adaptation episodes of the pointing phase (Fig. 1; text reports exponential fits and ANOVA), and aftereffect from the five pointing episodes without feedback (Fig. 1, open symbols). Numeric group means/SDs are shown only graphically in Fig. 1; the text gives exponential fit parameters (young y=9.92+53.51×exp(−x/5.89); old y=29.51+29.91×exp(−x/5.13)) and ANOVA statistics. Refresh phase and tracking transfer dropped (repeated exposure / context change).

roster.reason: Mean pointing errors ± SD for young and old across baseline, adaptation and after-effect episodes — carries the late adaptation and aftereffect values (graphically).
Tracking RMSE for the transfer phase and tracking-only controls — a different task/context, excluded by the protocol's dataset rules.
Parsing noise: the 'RESEARCH NOTES' header banner on page 1, not a data table.

parsed.notes: No supplementary material, appendix or data-availability statement is mentioned. The paper contains no numeric tables; all group time-series values appear only in Figs. 1 and 2, so the extraction pass may find no printed numbers for late adaptation and aftereffect other than the exponential fit parameters and ANOVA statistics in the Results text.
